drivers.driver: The institution's culture and governance failures have caused durable damage to the competitive franchise [D01, D05].
Persistent regulatory asset caps and ongoing remediation costs structurally constrain future earnings [D03].
The original thesis of a sound, disciplined banking franchise is no longer supported by observable customer or operating outcomes [D01, D07].

final.memo:
When we look at a business, we look for an enduring economic advantage and honest management that acts like an owner. In the case of this bank, the facts have changed fundamentally. The sales-practices scandal and the subsequent years of governance failures demonstrate that the institution lost its way, and restoring trust is a long, expensive, and uncertain process [D01, D05]. 

We do not hold businesses when the competitive advantage—the 'moat'—has been compromised by institutional rot [D01]. The regulatory asset restriction imposed in 2018 is not merely a temporary market fluctuation, but a binding constraint on our ability to grow our capital effectively [D03, D07]. We have seen significant management turnover and declining margins compared to our other financial holdings, which confirms that the business we thought we bought is not the business that exists today [D01, D03, D06]. 

We have already been reducing our stake, and it is time to conclude the exit [D07, D08]. We do not anchor on our original cost or wait for a price recovery when the underlying economic reality has deteriorated this significantly [D04, D05]. We prefer to allocate our capital to businesses where the future is more knowable and the managers are beyond reproach [D01, D04].
